- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above immediate prior high.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 65–70 range, adjust forecast toward center of recent 7-day window.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms when sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.33/1.00); use weighted average of 14-day and 30-day moving averages to smooth.
- If sentiment history shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00), model often fails to capture breakout; add 1–3% buffer to forecast for breakout potential.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model tends to drift downward; apply upward bias of 0.5–1.0% to prevent premature decline.
